newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil seeks role in new Moscow oil firm.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil seeks role in new Moscow oil firm.

text.p: Russian oil company LUKoil wants an active role in the newly-formed Central Fuel Company, LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov said on Friday.
"A passive role (in the new company) does not interest us...Of course, we would like to have conditions in place which would allow us not just to watch over the process," he told a news briefing.
But he also said LUKoil was not looking to take full control of Russia's newest energy company.

President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree on Wednesday ordering the transfer to the Moscow city government of 38 percent stakes in oil products trader Mosnefteprodukt and in the Moscow Oil Refinery, creating the Central Fuel Company.
LUKoil has said it owns more than 20 percent of voting shares in Mosnefteprodukt, a distributor of petroleum products.
The Moscow Oil Refinery is now managed by Rosneft, the state oil holding company which is now being privatised.
